card.name: Spots where "president" comes next
card.fires_on: Words and digits in political text just before or inside a mention of a president, such as "the", "first", "President" or a date after "served as president". It is strongest in history and news about heads of state.

modes.label: Dates after a president's term
modes.description: Digits in a year range right after a sentence naming someone who served as president.

modes.label: Before the title President
modes.description: The word "the" or "President" right before a president's office or name, often in a contrast with prime minister.
modes.example: Hitler decided to run against<< President>> Paul von Hindenburg. No one won

modes.label: Ex-president and office wording
modes.description: Linking words or hyphenated forms around ex-president, presidential palace or presidential elections.
modes.example: Polish ex<<-president>> Lech Walesa hailed Margaret Thatcher for

card.writes: It pushes the model toward president and presidential and away from minister, ministry and cabinet.
card.plain: It marks places in political text where the head of state, not a minister, is the likely next word.
